facts.fact: According to a figure cited by the page from PostAffiliatePro, acquiring a new customer can cost 5 to 25 times more than retaining an existing one.
facts.quote: Acquiring a new customer can cost [5 to 25 times more than retaining an existing one](https://www.postaffiliatepro.com/blog/why-customer-retention-costs-5x-less-than-acquisition/).

facts.fact: The page recommends building three automated email flows first: welcome, repeat-purchase, and lapsed-customer.
facts.quote: Build three automated flows first.

facts.fact: The page recommends a 60-day pilot when starting a small-business loyalty program.
facts.quote: Start with a 60-day pilot.

facts.fact: The page suggests that for many local businesses the first loyalty reward should be reachable within 30 to 90 days.
facts.quote: For many local businesses, that means a benefit customers can reach in 30 to 90 days.

facts.fact: The page recommends tracking four loyalty program metrics weekly: enrollment rate, reward redemption rate, repeat purchase rate, and average spend of members versus non-members.
facts.quote: Track four numbers weekly.

facts.fact: The page's loyalty implementation plan has five steps: set the goal, set the reward threshold, pick margin-protecting rewards, train staff and add prompts, and track four numbers weekly.
facts.quote: **Step 1: Set the goal.**

facts.fact: Small Business Expo, a third-party source, states that local businesses can reduce churn by 15% to 20% through referral loops and cross-industry loyalty partnerships.
facts.quote: local businesses can reduce churn by 15% to 20% through strategic referral loops and cross-industry loyalty partnerships

facts.fact: The page estimates that setting up a win-back sequence takes 2 to 4 hours of work to define segments, write the sequence, and build the triggers.
facts.quote: Expect 2 to 4 hours to define segments, write the sequence, and build the triggers.

facts.fact: The page says that hiring a freelancer for a win-back sequence is often a low three-figure project rather than a major campaign build.
facts.quote: this is often a low three-figure project, not a major campaign build.

facts.fact: The page states that a basic community content program can run with one staff member spending 30 to 45 minutes per week on the process.
facts.quote: one staff member owns the process for 30 to 45 minutes per week.

facts.fact: The page says the win-back approach is a four-step sequence that works well for most local businesses.
facts.quote: A practical four-step sequence works well for most local businesses

facts.fact: Adwave, per its own page, creates ads in minutes from a website URL.
facts.quote: The platform creates ads in minutes from a website URL

facts.fact: Adwave, per its own page, places ads across 100+ premium channels including NBC, Hulu, and ESPN.
facts.quote: places them across 100+ premium channels including NBC, Hulu, and ESPN

facts.fact: Adwave, per its own page, starts TV advertising campaigns at $30 a day.
facts.quote: campaigns start at $30 a day

facts.fact: Adwave's page gives an estimated CPM of $15 to $35 for its TV advertising.
facts.quote: with an estimated $15 to $35 CPM

facts.fact: Adwave's customer service article says SMBs can often run better support with existing tools or light software, typically $0 to $150 per month for shared inbox, chat, or ticketing support.
facts.quote: Most SMBs can do this with existing tools or light software costs, usually from $0 to $150 per month if they add shared inbox, chat, or ticketing support.

facts.fact: Adwave's content marketing section says content costs about $0 if the owner writes drafts, or roughly $150 to $500 per month if a freelancer edits and repurposes them.
facts.quote: Costs can stay near $0 if the owner writes drafts, or roughly $150 to $500 per month if a freelancer edits and repurposes them.

facts.fact: A third-party claim cited by Adwave (rivo.io) states that increasing customer retention by 5% can boost profits by 25% to 95%.
facts.quote: Increasing customer retention by 5% can boost profits by 25% to 95%, and repeat customers spend about 67% more over time

facts.fact: A third-party claim cited by Adwave (rivo.io) states that repeat customers spend about 67% more over time.
facts.quote: repeat customers spend about 67% more over time

facts.fact: Adwave recommends a service-rules approach of three or four rules followed consistently rather than a long policy document.
facts.quote: Three or four service rules followed consistently will outperform a long policy document nobody checks.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends a content publishing rhythm of two helpful pieces per month for many local businesses.
facts.quote: Two helpful pieces per month is enough for many local businesses.

facts.fact: Adwave's content plan suggests listing 10 to 20 recurring customer questions as the starting point for educational content.
facts.quote: List 10 to 20 recurring questions

facts.fact: Adwave's service implementation plan suggests auditing the last 20 customer issues in week one.
facts.quote: Week one, audit the last 20 customer issues and look for delays, repeat complaints, and handoff failures.

facts.fact: The page states that a small local business can often set up basic retention partnership materials and tracking for between $0 and $300 in direct cost.
facts.quote: In many cases, the direct cost is $0 to $300 to set up basic flyers, landing page copy, front-desk training, and a simple tracking sheet.

facts.fact: Adwave's page cites Bain & Company research summary claiming that a 5% increase in customer retention can raise profits by 25% to 95%.
facts.quote: Research summarized by Bain & Company shows that a 5% increase in customer retention can raise profits by 25% to 95%
